title: Wood Provision: Monetary Valuation
text:
This page is the second phase of the wood provision update. The first phase (physical accounts) produced the net annual increment (NAI) of forest available for wood supply (FAWS) by country and year, and mapped it. This page gives that flow a monetary value, expresses it in constant prices and maps it.
The method is the one of INCA Part III (La Notte et al., 2021) as implemented in the INCA plugin, so that results are comparable with it. It needs three Eurostat inputs and one deflator.

Value of standing timber. for_sup_cp reports the output of forest trees (P1_TR) in million euro (Eurostat, 2026c). Dividing it by NAI gives a unit value in euro per cubic metre. It is reported by few countries in the early years.
Unit value of roundwood exports. for_basic reports export value and volume of roundwood (Eurostat, 2026b). It is reported by almost every country and year.
Ratio between the two. Where both unit values exist, their ratio links the well-covered export price to the sparse timber price. The ratio is completed with averages and applied backwards: unit value of NAI = export unit value / ratio.
Deflator. The EU27 Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) converts nominal values to constant prices (Eurostat, 2026a).

The physical flow is not recomputed here. The page reads the tables that the first phase exported to data/outputs/results/, so both documents stay consistent.






ImportantRun the physical document first



This page reads data/outputs/results/wood_nai_faws_country_year.rds and the 1 km FAWS shares in data/inputs/faws/. Both are committed to the repository, so nothing needs to be rerun unless the physical series changes.








NoteConstant prices use a single base year



The base year is base_year in the parameters chunk. It is set to 2010, the base year of the fish provision accounts, so that the services share one price level (the INCA plugin uses 2000). Changing it does not touch the nominal values, because the deflator is applied in one step at the end.

title: Wood Provision: Monetary Valuation
text:
Parameters
The averages that complete the gaps use the same windows as the INCA plugin: the country mean over the whole series, and the EU mean over the more recent years, where coverage is better. The plugin stops at 2021 because of the data it had; the window here runs to 2023, the last year with broad coverage.

years_all <- 2000:2024
years_report <- c(2000, 2006, 2012, 2018, 2024)
base_year <- 2010

# Windows for the averages that fill gaps
country_years <- 2000:2023
eu_years <- 2012:2023

# Inputs
nai_file <- "data/outputs/results/wood_nai_faws_country_year.rds"
sup_file <- "data/inputs/eurostat/for_sup_cp_p1tr.rds"
basic_file <- "data/inputs/eurostat/for_basic_rw_exports.rds"
hicp_file <- "data/inputs/eurostat/hicp_eu27.rds"
countries_file <- "data/inputs/gis/NUTS_RG_01M_2024_3035_LEVL0.gpkg"
faws_share_file <- "data/inputs/faws/FAWS_2020_EU27_1km.tif"

# Outputs
results_dir <- "data/outputs/results"
gis_dir <- "data/outputs/gis"
dir.create(results_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(gis_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

title: Wood Provision Ecosystem Service
text:
The spatial key
Chapter 4 of INCA Part II spreads national flows with a productivity proxy over the forest classes of Corine Land Cover, and it explains that a map of forest available for wood supply did not exist at the time (Vallecillo et al., 2019). That map now exists (European Commission, Joint Research Centre, 2026). The routine uses it as the spatial key: inside each country, the national NAI is spread in proportion to the share of every 1 km cell that is available for wood supply. Cells without FAWS get no flow, and the cells of a country add up to its national value.
The FAWS map describes a single year (2020), so the same spatial key is used for every reporting year. Changes between years come only from the national statistics.

faws_share <- rast(faws_share_file)
eu_countries <- vect(countries_file)
eu_countries <- eu_countries[eu_countries$eu27, ]

title: Wood Provision Ecosystem Service
Wood Provision Ecosystem Service
text:
Spreading the national NAI
For each reporting year, the helper spread_totals() multiplies every cell by its country factor (national NAI divided by the weight total of the country). The result is in thousand cubic metres per 1 km cell, and each year is saved as a compressed GeoTIFF in data/outputs/gis/.

for (yr in years_report) {
  flow_map <- spread_totals(
    totals = filter(nai_filled, year == yr),
    weight = faws_share,
    country_ids = country_ids,
    weight_sums = weight_sums
  )
  names(flow_map) <- paste0("nai_faws_", yr)
  writeRaster(
    flow_map,
    file.path(gis_dir, sprintf("wood_nai_faws_1km_%s.tif", yr)),
    overwrite = TRUE,
    datatype = "FLT4S",
    gdal = c("COMPRESS=DEFLATE", "PREDICTOR=3", "TILED=YES")
  )
}

title: Wood Provision Ecosystem Service
text:
Why and how
The baseline uses the 2020 FAWS pattern for every year. Corine Land Cover (CLC) maps forest for 2000, 2006, 2012 and 2018 (European Environment Agency, 2020), so combining the two lets the spatial key change with forest extent. The refined key of a year is the 100 m overlap of FAWS and CLC forest (broad-leaved, coniferous and mixed forest, CLC 311, 312 and 313) of that epoch, summed to 1 km shares. The national NAI is spread over it in the same way as in the baseline, so the sum of each country is conserved. CLC 2018 is the latest epoch and is also used for 2024.
The CLC rasters are 3 GB each as downloaded. The script scripts/05_prepare_clc.R reduces them to four 1 km files of about 9 MB in data/inputs/corine/. The version used is V2020_20u1 (the Copernicus Land Monitoring Service release that revised all epochs consistently).

source("scripts/05_prepare_clc.R", encoding = "UTF-8")

Spreading the national NAI

for (yr in years_report) {
  epoch <- clc_for_year[[as.character(yr)]]
  refined_map <- spread_totals(
    totals = filter(nai_filled, year == yr),
    weight = clc_weights[[epoch]],
    country_ids = country_ids,
    weight_sums = clc_weight_sums[[epoch]]
  )
  names(refined_map) <- paste0("nai_clc_", yr)
  writeRaster(
    refined_map,
    file.path(refine_gis_dir, sprintf("corine_refinement_wood_nai_faws_1km_%s.tif", yr)),
    overwrite = TRUE,
    datatype = "FLT4S",
    gdal = c("COMPRESS=DEFLATE", "PREDICTOR=3", "TILED=YES")
  )
}

The conservation check reads the files back, as in the baseline.

refined_maps <- rast(
  file.path(refine_gis_dir, sprintf("corine_refinement_wood_nai_faws_1km_%s.tif", years_report))
)

tibble(
  Year = years_report,
  `CLC epoch` = unname(clc_for_year[as.character(years_report)]),
  `Sum of maps (million m3)` = global(refined_maps, "sum", na.rm = TRUE)[[1]] / 1000,
  `Sum of national values (million m3)` = national_totals
) |>
  mutate(
    `Difference (%)` = 100 * (`Sum of maps (million m3)` / `Sum of national values (million m3)` - 1)
  ) |>
  show_table(digits = 2)
